To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a virtual sectorization scheme in a realistic LTE network can provide a significant increase in network capacity, while maintaining a good user experience, (2) the capacity gain depends on the chosen resource sharing scheme (power or spectrum) and the specific deployment of virtual sector(s), and (3) the SON algorithms developed in this thesis work are able to dynamically optimize the network configuration for the given deployment, resource sharing scheme and network conditions, and hence maximize the network capacity.
the use of ViS is beneficial in terms of capacity and user experience.
• Virtual Sectorization can provide a significant increase of the network capacity, while keeping the same number of base stations.

the study, design and evaluation of the ViS concept, and the development and optimization of SON algorithms that can be employed to dynamically share the spectrum and/or power resources between virtual cells and the macro-cell.
the study of ViS in LTE networks, with focus on system-level capacity assessment, performance analysis and optimization of ViS.
the development of a SON solution that is capable of optimizing the deployment of ViSe in an LTE network in order to improve network performance.

the ViS approach is a viable option to be considered in order to cope with increasing mobile traffic.
